dailyTopNewsBrief.headline: Buccaneers Fall to 3-7 After 31-21 Loss in Detroit
dailyTopNewsBrief.summary: Tampa Bay drops to 3-7 following a 31-21 road defeat against the Detroit Lions, leaving their playoff probability at 32.5% heading into Week 12. Despite fielding the NFL's top-ranked rushing attack, pass protection vulnerabilities continue to hamper offensive efficiency.
bullets: Quarterback Baker Mayfield absorbed four sacks during Sunday's 31-21 defeat, underscoring ongoing pass protection issues for an offense ranking #30 in sack rate allowed (10.1%), per [buccaneers.com Official](https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-lions-week-11-recap-postgame-report-2026).

Head coach Todd Bowles oversees an extreme statistical divide, as Tampa Bay ranks #1 in rushing (163.9 yards per game) but #32 in passing offense (141.9 yards per game), noted via [buccaneers.com Video](https://www.buccaneers.com/video/todd-bowles-on-outcome-in-detroit-press-conference).

Detroit pulled away late with two fourth-quarter rushing touchdowns from Jahmyr Gibbs, breaking through a Tampa Bay defense that otherwise leads the NFL in run defense (79.1 yards allowed per game), according to [ESPN NFL Nation](https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401873072).

Linebacker Alex Anzalone and the defense turn focus to Week 12 against the 5-5 Carolina Panthers, who bring the league's #8 passing attack (252.8 yards per game) to Tampa, per [buccaneers.com Video](https://www.buccaneers.com/video/alex-anzalone-discusses-first-game-back-in-detroit-press-conference).
